The question asks for the smallest order $n$ at which two non-isoclinic groups can have isomorphic conjugacy quandles. I did not derive this or check it computationally, so the answer relies on my recollection of the literature on conjugacy quandles and isoclinism, which I hold with moderate confidence.

Isoclinic groups have isomorphic conjugacy quandles, so the question concerns the converse. The conjugacy quandle $\mathrm{Conj}(G)$ records the conjugation action on $G$, which determines the inner automorphism group and the commutator structure. Isoclinism is a finer relation tied to the central quotient and the commutator map, so for small orders the two notions appear to coincide. I recall that the first counterexamples to the converse occur at order 32.

ANSWER: 32
